results.title: Harmeet Dhillon resigns as DOJ's assistant attorney general for civil rights: sources | Fox News
results.summary:
Summary:
- The Fox News report indicates Harmeet Dhillon, who served as head of the Department of Justice Civil Rights Division, formally resigned on November 5, following her swearing-in in April 2025 after being nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate in April 2025.
- The piece notes internal turnover within the Civil Rights Division during her tenure and describes her as a high-profile figure in First Amendment, election law, and civil-rights litigation.
- The article frames the resignation as part of post-midterm personnel shifts but does not detail a cabinet-level or White House senior official resignation, firing, or nomination tied to the 2026 midterms.

If you’re tracking cabinet/White House-level moves after the 2026 midterms, this article does not document a cabinet secretary, senior White House official, or equivalent figure resigning, being fired, or being nominated in the aftermath. It relates specifically to Harmeet Dhillon’s resignation from a DOJ leadership role earlier in 2025.
